definition: The micturition reflex is the body reflex involved in urination. In the source material, it is described as a reflex that can be suppressed, which is associated with reduced urinary bladder contraction and increased bladder capacity.

provenance.scope: Source record C61765; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define the micturition reflex itself; it describes flavoxate, a drug that suppresses the reflex.
The statement that it is a ‘body reflex involved in urination’ is not supported by the supplied text.
The added description about reduced bladder contraction and increased bladder capacity is presented as an effect of flavoxate in the packet, not as a defining property of the reflex.
The packet does not explicitly define what the “micturition reflex” is as a body reflex involved in urination; it only describes how flavoxate suppresses “the micturition reflex.”
Because the core definition of the term (beyond the idea that it can be suppressed) is not stated in the packet, the first sentence’s characterization is not fully supported by the provided text.
